lesson: In GOAP-based AI systems, interrupt evaluation often triggers expensive plan computation that is only used for freely-interruptible actions. Guard plan computation behind interruptibility checks to avoid wasteful search.

When GOAP search consistently exhausts budget for specific goals, track them and skip re-search until the world changes in ways that could make the goal plannable (position, inventory, wounds). Needs-only changes rarely alter search space.

POSITION dirty bit aggressively clears the search_exhausted_goals cache during multi-leg travel. Tracking last_in_transit state and only clearing when the agent genuinely arrives (transit-to-settled transition) preserves the cache across waypoints, avoiding redundant GOAP searches.

For GOAP planners with budget-limited search, track goals that previously exhausted the budget. When the exhausted-goals cache is cleared (due to world changes), re-search these goals with a reduced budget (e.g., 50%) since they are likely to exhaust again. This preserves the ability to find plans while reducing wasted computation on chronically unsolvable goals.

Exponential backoff on GOAP search budget (halving per exhaustion, floor at 64) is more effective than a flat reduction. Chronically unsolvable goals get searched with minimal effort (87.5% reduction after 3 failures) while preserving plan-finding ability. Clear exhaustion counts when a plan IS found to reset the penalty.
